record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n-1, 3n) for n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
With T (n) = T112 (3n - 1, 3n) with n >= 1, it appears that T (n) has no prime factor greater than or equal to 4n.
Problem 11: Find a formula governing T112 (3n - 1, 3n). See OEIS entry A364483.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular grid in the plane. For positive integers $a, b$, define the $(a,b)$-benzel as the region obtained from the triangular grid by removing all unit triangles whose centroid lies "too far" in a specified way (the standard benzel region with parameters $a, b$, having three-fold rotational symmetry, used in the study of trimer tilings on the hexagonal lattice). A trimer is a tile covering three adjacent unit triangles. There are two stone orientations (left stone and right stone, each formed by three triangles meeting at a vertex) and three bone orientations (each a row of three triangles aligned along one of the three lattice directions).

For $i, j \in \{0,1\}$ and $k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel using only prototiles drawn from the following allowed set: the right stone is allowed iff $i = 1$, the left stone is allowed iff $j = 1$, and exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations are allowed (with the choice of which $k$ bone orientations being fixed by convention up to symmetry).

Define
$$T(n) = T_{112}(3n-1, 3n) \quad \text{for } n \geq 1.$$
That is, $T(n)$ counts tilings of the $(3n-1, 3n)$-benzel using both stone orientations and exactly two of the three bone orientations.

Find a closed-form formula (or explicit product/recurrence) for $T(n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as Problem 11 in a recent (2023) list of mostly open problems on trimer covers in the triangular grid by Kim and Propp, with the corresponding OEIS entry A364483 cataloging the computed values. No published formula has been found in searches; the empirical observation is only that $T(n)$ has no prime factor $\geq 4n$. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Jim Propp's Benzel Tilings Site
status_evidence.snippet: Page listing problems and computations on benzel tilings, including trimer tilings and references to OEIS sequences such as A364483.
status_evidence.claim: The benzel problems list is maintained on Propp's site, indicating the problems remain open as research topics.

status_evidence.title: A Pentagonal Number Theorem for Tribone Tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper by Kim and Propp on tribone tilings of benzels.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats the k=3 case; the k=2 case for T112(3n-1,3n) is not addressed with a closed formula.
